diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then there exists a constant $\zeta > 0$ such that for every $z \in \cS$, one can find a point $y \in \cY$ (possibly depending on $z$) satisfying $\bc(y, z) \leq -\zeta$.
By this and Theorem~\ref{thm:UniSlater},  there exists $\hat{y}^k \in \cY$ such that $\bc(\hat{y}^k, z^k) \leq -\zeta < 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The negation of the theorem's conclusion yields: for every $\zeta>0$ there is $z\in\cS$ such that for every $y\in\cY$ SOME component $j$ (depending on $y$) has $\bc_j(y,z)>-\zeta$; equivalently, with $A_j^k=\{y\in\cY:\bc_j(y,z^k)\le-\zeta_k\}$, only $\bigcap_{j=1}^m A_j^k=\emptyset$ is available. The proof instead asserts one fixed $j$ with $\bc_j(y,z^k)>-\zeta_k$ for all $y\in\cY$ and all $k$, i.e., that a single $A_j^k$ is empty. This quantifier exchange is invalid: each $A_j^k$ is closed convex (an intersection of $\cY$ with a Euclidean ball, since $\bc_j(\cdot,z)$ is a convex quadratic in its first argument), and finitely many nonempty closed convex sets can have empty intersection (e.g., two disjoint intervals), so no such $j$ need exist. The rest of the proof (passage to the limit, $c_j(z)=0$, and the MFCQ-based directional contradiction) depends on this single $j$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid single-$j$ extraction with a direct contradiction: along $z^k\to z\in\cS$, for each fixed $y\in\cY$ a subsequence/pigeonhole argument gives some $j(y)$ with $\bc_{j(y)}(y,z)\ge0$; but MFCQ at $z$ provides $\tz\in\cY$ such that $y(t)=z+t(\tz-z)\in\cY$ satisfies $\bc_j(y(t),z)<0$ for every $j$ and all small $t>0$ — a contradiction. This contained rewriting preserves the theorem and all downstream results verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the uniform Slater property of $\bc$ is unproved, which compromises the written proofs of the Lagrange-multiplier bounds (lambda-bound, lambda-uniform-bound) and, transitively, the SCP rate/termination results (lem:added-1, thm:sub_iters) and the complexity guarantees for Algorithm 2 (lem:subsolver_output, lem:gen_converge, thm:outer_bound, thm:operations). The statement itself is true (a repaired argument exists), so the damage is to the proofs as written and is fully restorable.

The proof follows from Theorems~\ref{thm:Phi_localHolder}, \ref{thm:Phi_QG}, and \ref{thm:sub_iters}, along with arguments similar to those used in the proof of  \cite[Lemma~9]{lu2025first}.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion at $\ell=k$ concerns $y^k$, which is the output of the SCP call at outer iteration $k-1$ on the subproblem at $x^k$ initialized at $y^{k-1}$. Applying thm:sub_iters to that call requires the SCP input condition $h(y^{k-1})\le h^*+\eta$, i.e., $F^*(x^k)-F(x^k,y^{k-1})\le\gamma\dist(0,\partial\bPsi(x^k))^\sigma$ (the only KL level for the subproblem guaranteed by Assumption 1(iv)). The inductive quality of $y^{k-1}$ plus the trust region $\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|\le r$ only yield $F^*(x^k)-F(x^k,y^{k-1})\le\gamma\epsilon^\sigma$, which is $\le\gamma\dist(0,\partial\bPsi(x^k))^\sigma$ only when $\dist(0,\partial\Psi(x^k))\ge\epsilon$ (i.e., $x^k\in\cU_\epsilon$). The hypotheses cover $x^\ell\in\cX^c_\epsilon$ only for $\ell<k$, so the premise for the call producing $y^k$ is never established. The conclusion at $\ell=k$ can genuinely fail: if $x^k\in\cX_\epsilon$ (allowed by the hypotheses), the KL level can be far below the initial gap, and the SCP may terminate at a spurious stationary point of the inner problem (such points exist; see the paper's own Example), violating \eqref{lem9-ineq1-1}. Consequently the $y^k$-quality claims \eqref{yk-opt} in thm:outer_bound are not guaranteed at the reported terminal iterate, and in that case the terminal SCP call also has no iteration bound, so the oracle count $\widehat N_\epsilon$ in thm:operations is not guaranteed either.
